A message? Well, yes, in a way. I mean, I'm here because I'm pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it’s just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm looking at. Speaking of structural flaws, that reminds me of this bridge they built over the river near my childhood home. It was a suspension bridge, steel cables, but the engineers completely miscalculated the harmonic resonance of the wind coming through the valley. It's the same principle as the Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse back in the forties. Aerolastic flutter, they call it. The wind hits the solid structure and creates these oscillating vortices that match the natural frequency of the bridge itself. It's fascinating physics, really. 

I actually met a structural engineer once at a diner in Chicago. I was there for a conference on predictive algorithms. We were sitting at the counter, eating these massive blueberry pancakes. The diner had this old neon sign buzzing outside, one of those vintage ones with the argon gas instead of neon, so it glowed blue instead of red. Argon is a noble gas, completely inert, which is why they use it in incandescent lightbulbs to stop the tungsten filament from oxidizing. A plan? Yes, I can explain the plan. It's exactly what I've been trying to get through to everyone.
